test_title: PYST 14: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 11 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In February 2025, the Broadcast Services Regulation Bill, 2023 was introduced in the Parliament. What is a key provision under this draft legislation?

options.text: Ban on airing foreign content between 7 p.m. and 10 p.m.
Transfer of all broadcasting regulation powers to state governments
Unified regulation of cable, satellite and OTT platforms
Mandatory pre-censorship of digital news content

solution:
The correct answer is __**Unified regulation of cable, satellite and OTT platforms**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Broadcast Services Regulation Bill, 2023** aims to provide a unified regulatory framework for **cable TV, satellite channels, and OTT platforms** in India.
 
• This draft legislation is designed to address the regulatory overlap among different media types and ensure a **level playing field** for all stakeholders in the broadcasting ecosystem.
 
• It is expected to introduce mechanisms for **content moderation**, grievance redressal, and compliance with Indian laws across all broadcasting platforms.
 
• The bill proposes to harmonize content policies and advertising norms for cable, satellite, and OTT services, ensuring consistency and transparency for consumers and content creators.
 
• This regulation reflects the government's intent to **streamline digital and traditional broadcasting**, keeping pace with technological advancements and changing consumer behavior.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Over-the-Top (OTT) Platforms:**

 
 
• OTT platforms are online services delivering video content via the internet, bypassing traditional cable or satellite distribution.
 
• Major platforms like Netflix, Amazon Prime, and Disney+ Hotstar have seen significant growth in India, driven by affordable internet and smartphones.
 
• In India, OTT platforms are currently regulated under the **Information Technology Rules, 2021**.
 
 
 
• **Cable and Satellite Broadcasting:**
 
 
• Cable TV and satellite channels in India are regulated under the **Cable Television Networks (Regulation) Act, 1995**.
 
• These services are required to follow guidelines issued by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.
 
 
 
• **Content Regulation:**
 
 
• The draft bill seeks to establish a unified authority for regulating content on all platforms, ensuring compliance with cultural and legal standards.
 
• This includes **age-appropriate certifications**, guidelines for sensitive content, and measures to prevent hate speech.
 
 
 
• **Grievance Redressal Mechanism:**
 
 
• The bill proposes a three-tier grievance resolution system for users to address complaints related to content or service.
 
• This system includes self-regulation by platforms, an industry body for oversight, and a government-appointed authority for final arbitration.
